Qel-Droma believed that he was going crazy; however, the girl called out to him and revealed herself to be Nomi Sunrider's daughter, Vima. The young Sunrider asked Qel-Droma to train her as a Jedi, but Qel-Droma refused, on account that he no longer had a connection to the Force. Although Sunrider fought him every step of the way, Qel-Droma did not budge, and he eventually threw her out of his hideaway and commanded her to return home. However, Sunrider, stuck in the middle of a blizzard, could not contact anyone for help. Qel-Droma took pity on his would-be apprentice and ventured out into the storm. Qel-Droma eventually found her, and relied on her Force sense to find them a shelter in the Rhen Var wilderness. The two talked while huddled around a light, and although Qel-Droma warned Sunrider of the cost of being a Jedi&mdash;drawing on his own experiences to do so&mdash;Sunrider still wanted to learn from him, even though he had no connection to the Force. Qel-Droma reluctantly agreed to teach her in the ways of the Force, to complete the training that Sunrider's mother had neglected.<ref name="redemption3" />

Although Qel-Droma no longer had any Jedi powers, he taught Vima Sunrider everything he knew. Sunrider displayed tremendous dedication and progressed very quickly. Her dedication surprised Qel-Droma, who remarked that he had never seen such commitment in a student. After some time with Sunrider, Qel-Droma decided that it was time for her to build her first [[Vima Sunrider's lightsaber|lightsaber]]&mdash;she did so successfully through the use of [[Adegan crystal/Legends|Adegan crystals]] that had belonged to her father, a Jedi Knight named [[Andur Sunrider]]. They promptly sparred for the first time, and although he could not feel the Force, Qel-Droma discovered that he still possessed his lightsaber skills. Afterward, as Sunrider continued to practice with her lightsaber, Qel-Droma abruptly told her that he could not teach her anymore, as he was no longer a Jedi. Qel-Droma compared his situation to a blinded painter, to which Sunrider replied that he should become a sculptor, to feel his way where he could no longer see. Exasperated by his pupil's logic, Qel-Droma agreed to try sculpturing, literally. The two found an ice-covered mountain and erected a large scaffolding from which to ply their craft. Qel-Droma and Sunrider both began their own works&mdash;while Sunrider used the Force to guide her, Qel-Droma used his own skill. Qel-Droma carved a sculpture of Master Arca Jeth into the mountain, while Sunrider created one of her father. They successfully made perfect likenesses of their respective subjects, and Qel-Droma felt that he had finally suitably honored his Jedi Master.<ref name="redemption4">[[Tales of the Jedi – Redemption 4|''Tales of the Jedi – Redemption'' 4]]</ref>

====Death====
{{Quote|Of all the people to free me from my anger&hellip; it was ''you.''<nowiki></nowiki>|Sylvar, to Ulic Qel-Droma|<ref name="redemption5" />}}
[[File:BlastedUlic.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Ulic Qel-Droma is fatally shot.]]
During one lightsaber training session with his young apprentice, Qel-Droma took the opportunity to teach Sunrider a lesson on the burdens of being a Jedi, including the life-and-death choices that were inherent with the title of Jedi Knight. Afterward, Qel-Droma and Sunrider returned to the fortress&mdash;as they walked through the door, however, Sunrider sensed that her mother Nomi was on her way to the citadel. Nomi promptly entered, and demanded that Vima return home with her. When Qel-Droma turned around, he and his former love were face-to-face for the first time in years. Although Vima resisted and defended Qel-Droma as a teacher, Qel-Droma recognized that it was Nomi's decision and left it up to her to determine what to do with her daughter. Albeit reluctantly, Nomi yielded to Vima's pleas and decided to give her a chance to show what she had learned from Qel-Droma. Vima took her mother to the sculptures of Arca Jeth and Andur Sunrider that Qel-Droma and her had made together, while Qel-Droma remained behind in his citadel. While alone, Qel-Droma silently thanked Jeth for convincing him that he should live, and although the past still weighed heavily upon him, Qel-Droma thought that he could perhaps find peace. However, at that point, Qel-Droma was called out to by [[Sylvar]], a Cathar Jedi and the former mate of Crado, who desperately wanted revenge for her lover's death and had tracked Qel-Droma to Rhen Var. Although Qel-Droma asked Sylvar to let go of her anger as he had done his guilt, Sylvar still attacked him and engaged him in a [[Duel on Rhen Var|lightsaber duel]].<ref name="redemption5" />

As the two battled, Qel-Droma refused to be the aggressor, and instead settled for blocking Sylvar's furious blows as he continued to ask her to move on from Crado's death. They dueled their way up to a narrow catwalk, and although Qel-Droma pleaded for Sylvar to bury her past, the Cathar responded that Qel-Droma had not been punished enough for what he did during the Sith War. Sylvar eventually backed Qel-Droma to the edge of a steep ledge, and as Qel-Droma faced death, he deactivated his lightsaber and refused to fight anymore. Although Sylvar, whom Qel-Droma had called a pawn to her own emotions, had a chance to finish Qel-Droma off, she too put away her weapon&mdash;Qel-Droma had freed her from her anger. Suddenly, however, a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] bolt ripped through Qel-Droma's back. The shot was fired by the spacer [[Hoggon]], whom Sylvar had enlisted to take her to Rhen Var, and who saw his chance to make history by killing who he saw as one of the greatest war criminals of all time. Although Hoggon was quickly sent on his way by Sylvar, Qel-Droma was fatally wounded. In his last moments, Qel-Droma asked Nomi Sunrider to forgive him&mdash;Sunrider told the dying Qel-Droma to rest easy, as she had already done so. He also gave Vima a [[Necklace/Legends|necklace]] that he wore, and thanked her for helping him find peace as he called her a Jedi for the first time. With that, Ulic Qel-Droma passed away, in Nomi Sunrider's arms. Redeemed, Qel-Droma's body disappeared as was the way of Jedi Masters, and he moved to the Netherworld of the Force.<ref name="redemption5" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|The knowledge you seek is very powerful, Anakin Skywalker, use it carefully, or it will lead you to the dark side.''"<br />"''I am not afraid.''"<br />"''You should be. I once thought I was impervious to the allure of the dark side. I was mistaken. Do not take the same path as I.|Ulic Qel-Droma's spirit and Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="Clone Wars" />}}
[[File:Ulics_Tomb.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Ulic Qel-Droma's tomb on Rhen Var]]
Following Qel-Droma's death, a large [[Jedi monument (Rhen Var)|mausoleum]] was built in his honor on Rhen Var, and his coffin was placed within the monument. A trio of ghostly [[spectral guardian]]s were stationed in the mausoleum's antechamber, tasked with defending Qel-Droma's remains. Qel-Droma's Force ghost took up residency in his tomb.<ref name="Clone Wars" /> Due to his major part in [[Timeline of galactic history/Legends|galactic history]], Ulic Qel-Droma was remembered long after his death. In [[3980 BBY]], his former pupil Vima Sunrider recorded the story of his redemption onto the [[Great Holocron/Legends|Great Holocron]], the centerpiece of the [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]]<ref name="jvs" />&mdash;Sunrider went on to become a full-fledged Jedi Master.<ref name="kotorcg" /> Indeed, the Archives contained a wealth of information on Qel-Droma for centuries.<ref name="jvs" /> Qel-Droma's story was taught to Jedi apprentices such as [[Zayne Carrick]]<ref name="kotor8">[[Knights of the Old Republic 8|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 8]]</ref> and [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] in the time after Qel-Droma's death.<ref name="kotor">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> During the Republic's [[Mandalorian Wars|war]] with the Mandalorians several decades after Qel-Droma's time, Republic [[Propaganda/Legends|propaganda]] used Qel-Droma's defeat of Mandalore the Indomitable in single combat to try to demoralize Mandalorian warriors.<ref name="interference">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/fiction/interference20090929.html|text="Interference"|int=Interference|newhost=Suvudu}}</ref> Several centuries after Qel-Droma's death, when the Jedi Order and the Republic faced a new threat in the form of a resurgent [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], Jedi Master [[Gnost-Dural]] researched Qel-Droma, Kun, and the Great Sith War as part of a [[Galactic Timeline (in-universe)|timeline]] of galactic history.<ref name="timeline10">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 10: The Exar Kun War|int=Timeline 10: The Exar Kun War}}</ref>

Over time, the knowledge of the locations of the Dark Reaper and the Force Harvester became forgotten, even among the Jedi. Millennia later in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the Republic and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], the Sith Lord and leader of the Separatist movement [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] discovered the existence of the Dark Reaper. With the hopes of using the ancient Sith superweapon to destroy the Republic, Dooku had the Separatists [[Evacuation of Rhen Var|capture]] Rhen Var and Qel-Droma's tomb from the Republic.<ref name="Clone Wars" /> Upon learning the Force Harvester's location on Raxus Prime from Qel-Droma's spirit,<ref name="nec" /> Dooku had the Harvester dug up, and began to charge it using a number of unsuspecting Republic targets. The Jedi, having learned of Dooku's use of the Force Harvester after it was featured in a [[Battle on Alaris|battle]] on [[Alaris Prime/Legends|Alaris Prime]], dispatched Jedi Master [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and his Padawan [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], along with a large contingent of the Republic's [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|clone army]], to [[Battle of Rhen Var (Clone Wars)|recapture]] Rhen Var and uncover where the Dark Reaper was hidden so that the Jedi could destroy it. Skywalker managed to fight past the Separatist forces stationed there, as well as Qel-Droma's spectral guardians, and eventually entered Qel-Droma's tomb. There, Skywalker met with Qel-Droma's spirit, asking the long-dead Jedi about where the Dark Reaper was located and how to destroy it. Qel-Droma told the Padawan of the Reaper's burial on Thule, about how to resist the effects of the Force Harvester, and about how to destroy the Reaper. However, Qel-Droma warned Skywalker that resisting the Force Harvester required much power and might draw Skywalker closer to the dark side. With Qel-Droma's knowledge, the Republic launched an [[Battle of Thule|assault]] on Thule as Dooku began to unearth the superweapon. As he piloted a [[TX-130 Saber-class fighter tank/Legends|TX-130 fighter tank]], Skywalker single-handedly attacked the Reaper just as it became fully operational. Hearing Qel-Droma's voice as he fought, Skywalker managed to bypass the Reaper's defenses and destroy the Sith superweapon once and for all, finally finishing what Qel-Droma started thousands of years ago.<ref name="Clone Wars" /> Despite this victory, however, Anakin did indeed fall to the dark side three years later, just as Qel-Droma had warned, becoming the Sith Lord Darth Vader and once again brought about the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|near-destruction]] of the Jedi.<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref>

Millennia after his death on Rhen Var, Qel-Droma's story passed into legend, and his story became immortalized in a series of epic poems collectively known as the [[Qel-Droma Epics/Legends|Qel-Droma Epics]]. The center of study of the Qel-Droma Epics was the [[Great Library of Cinnagar/Legends|Great Library of Cinnagar]], which housed a museum dedicated to the stories, and many of the people of Empress Teta took the fanciful Epics as the literal history of the world. By the era of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the location of the Iron Citadel from which the Krath once ruled was lost, and some scholars of the Epics believed that Qel-Droma's lightsaber crystal could be found within the ancient structure. The Qel-Droma Epics also preserved many descriptions of the by then-lost Ossus before its destruction, and the spot where Qel-Droma slew his brother and was stripped of the Force became a powerful dark side Force [[Vergence/Legends|vergence]].<ref name="nexus of power">''[[Nexus of Power]]''</ref> In the year [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]], [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] member [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] came into possession of the [[Tedryn Holocron]], an ancient device that had existed since Qel-Droma's time<ref name="jvs" /> and had taught Exar Kun himself.<ref name="DLotS1" /> Solo was worried about [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], her brother and a Jedi Knight who had tried to defeat the dark side from within like Qel-Droma had. The holocron's gatekeeper, a representation of long-dead Jedi Master [[Bodo Baas]], told Solo the story of how Qel-Droma had tried the same by infiltrating the Krath, and how he fell to the dark side. The story stunned Solo, although she did not have enough time to hear the tale of Qel-Droma's redemption.<ref name="endnotes">[[Dark Empire endnotes|''Dark Empire'' endnotes]]</ref> One of Qel-Droma's descendants, a man by the name of [[Sedriss QL|Qaga Lok]], took the name Sedriss QL<ref name="ff">{{FactFile|85|SED 1-4|Exekutor Sedress (German Edition)}}</ref> and became a high-ranking [[Executor (Imperial rank)|Military Executor]] in the Galactic Empire, before his [[Skirmish on Ossus|death]] at the hands of Ood Bnar&mdash;who had survived the shockwave of the Cron Supernova and lived for four thousand more years&mdash;in 10 ABY.<ref name="nec" />

[[40 ABY/Legends|Thirty years later]], [[Jedi historian]] [[Tionne Solusar]] wrote a [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force|compendium]] about the Force, which contained several mentions of Qel-Droma. Specifically, it contained several anecdotes and essays about Qel-Droma, including Vima Sunrider's account of his redemption and works by the likes of Arca Jeth, Vodo-Siosk Baas, and Jedi Master [[Tolaris Shim]].<ref name="jvs" /> Qel-Droma was also mentioned in [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] [[archivist emeritus]] [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al's]] [[The New Essential Chronology (in-universe)|chronicle]] of galactic history.<ref name="nec" />

==Personality and traits==
===Jedi Knight===
{{Quote|Your brother lets courage cloud his mind!|Tott Doneeta, to Cay Qel-Droma|<ref name="beastwars1" />}}
[[File:TOTJ1-FC.jpg|thumb|left|225px|Ulic Qel-Droma the Jedi]]
In his younger days, Ulic Qel-Droma, a man of light skin, brown [[Hair/Legends|hair]], and brown eyes,<ref name="egtc" /> was pure of [[Heart/Legends|heart]] and purpose and completely uncorrupted. Although he came across to some as arrogant, those who were close to him could attest that he simply possessed unbounded confidence<ref name="endnotes" />&mdash;even to the point of overconfidence.<ref name="beastwars1" /> Qel-Droma was also very headstrong&mdash;he refused to back down from his position that infiltrating the Krath was the only way to deal with them<ref name="endnotes" />&mdash;impulsive, and impressionable.<ref name="makingswc">{{JournalCite|2|Making Star Wars Comics Come Alive|Making ''Star Wars'' Comics Come Alive}}</ref> According to his Jedi Master, Arca Jeth, he also let courage often cloud his mind.<ref name="audio" /> Qel-Droma lacked the ability to ignore the disdainful words of the Alderaanian nobles, which drove him to give his all in his academic and extracurricular pursuits.<ref name="totjcompanion" /> Easily frustrated when things did not go his way,<ref name="jatm" /> Qel-Droma always threw himself completely into his efforts, and believed that he could do a better job than any of his peers. However, he was very fickle with his projects, as he quickly became bored with them and shifted his attention to something else. Qel-Droma contained a great amount of personal pride, and refused to study the Force in his early years because he didn't want to be seen as having to ride his mother's coat-tails to succeed. When he discovered his talent in the Force, he was delighted and gained an increased self-confidence. During his Jedi training, Qel-Droma displayed a tendency to act before thinking, and he piqued concerns from his mother, a Jedi Master in her own right, that he had missed the underlying purpose of the Jedi Order.<ref name="totjcompanion" /> Qel-Droma's upbringing outside the Jedi Temple led to his naiveté regarding the dark side, which would end up being his undoing.<ref name="kotorcg" />

Qel-Droma held a great deal of respect for his Master, Arca Jeth, and believed him to always be right. Due to this, Qel-Droma greatly desired to prove to his Master that he was a worthy and courageous Jedi Knight, and he was headstrong enough that he would not be dissuaded from pursuing this goal.<ref name="beastwars1" /> Qel-Droma made it a point to follow Jeth's orders exactly, and when he failed to do so, he was very disappointed in himself.<ref name="beastwars2" /> Devoted to his Master, Qel-Droma was willing to die to protect him. Despite his boundless confidence in himself, Qel-Droma valued his duty as a Jedi above his own life, to the point that he took on dozens of Beast Riders by himself so Tott Doneeta and his brother Cay could save Queen Amanoa and Princess Galia on Onderon.<ref name="beastwars1" /> Qel-Droma had a deep bond with Cay and felt a duty to protect him, and even risked his life to retrieve him from the Iziz throne room during the Beast Wars. Qel-Droma had a very high view of the Jedi Order, and during his youth he did not think it possible for one to fall to the dark side.<ref name="beastwars2" /> As he became more experienced, he began to realize the threat that the dark side posed<ref name="uprising1" />&mdash;although he knew that the dark side was omnipresent in the galaxy, he did not lack the ability to push those facts out of his mind and be at leisure.<ref name="DLotS1" /> Qel-Droma did not outgrow his naive underestimation of the power of the dark side, believing that he could resist its dark lure.<ref name="DLotS3" />

Always bold, Qel-Droma was not easily frightened, and he even had the courage to challenge the dark spirit of Freedon Nadd when the ghost revealed itself to him on Onderon.<ref name="DLotS1" /> He was not without fear, however, as shown by his terrified reaction to the space grazers conjured by Aleema Keto during the first battle between the Republic and the Krath.<ref name="DLotS2" /> During the Conclave on Deneba, Qel-Droma showed himself as a believer in his own self-reliance, as he repeatedly refused help while climbing up a mountain to the Jedi convocation despite heavy injuries suffered in battle at Empress Teta.<ref name="audio" /> Despite his pride and boldness, this Jedi Knight could not help but blame himself for Arca Jeth's death on Deneba, as he believed that if he had been more aware of his surroundings he could have protected his aged teacher. This resulted in a major hit to his self-confidence, as he began to think that he was not a true Jedi; it also resulted in a grim determination to succeed in his quest to infiltrate the Krath, in order to honor his Master.<ref name="DLotS3" /> Always pragmatic, Qel-Droma developed contempt for Jedi who disagreed with his plan, and at one point called them "rank cowards" for not battling the dark side as he wanted to. He even became defiant toward venerable and respected Jedi Masters Odan-Urr and Ood Bnar, and saw them as complacent and not willing to destroy the dark side.<ref name="DLotS4" /> Qel-Droma could be very inquisitive and enjoyed asking his friend Doneeta about Twi'lek culture.<ref name="audio" />

===Sith Lord===
{{Quote|Ulic is lost to us&hellip; I can feel it&hellip;|Nomi Sunrider, to Cay Qel-Droma, after their first failed rescue attempt on Empress Teta|<ref name="DLotS5" />}}
[[File:Ulic_qel_droma.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Ulic Qel-Droma the Sith]]
After his encounter with the Krath, Qel-Droma changed completely; he became a powerful dark side warrior who led bloodthirsty and militaristic campaigns<ref name="endnotes" /> and spread death and disorder at a [[Speciecide|genocidal]] level.<ref name="desourcebook">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> At first, he still considered himself a member of the Jedi Order, but he cast his abhorrence of the dark side aside to pursue his mission inside the Krath.<ref name="DLotS4" /> Always committed to his goal, Qel-Droma was willing to do anything to keep his facade intact, even volunteering to execute his love, Nomi Sunrider. Although Qel-Droma still tried to adhere to the Jedi way while undercover, he was led astray by Aleema Keto and the Sith poison injected by Satal Keto. As Aleema undermined his determination with her seduction, the Sith poison multiplied and accentuated his rage, which drew him closer to the dark side. Qel-Droma became fiercely independent and directed his growing rage toward those who tried to help him. Eventually, that anger drove him to lash out at his brother and fellow Jedi, and although he was sorry for his violent actions toward them, he realized that he was on a path of no return to the dark side.<ref name="DLotS5" /> Though he denounced them as weak and complacent when confronted by his former friends, Qel-Droma yet held them in regard as good Jedi, but he still took Aleema Keto and the Krath over Nomi Sunrider and the Jedi when presented with the choice.<ref name="DLotS6" />

After his fall to the dark side, Qel-Droma's characteristic confidence and boldness remained, but with a significantly harder edge. He became devoted to his newfound dark side powers, although he never renounced his title as Jedi Knight, even after his full entrance into the Sith. This new Ulic Qel-Droma had no problems ordering the deaths of innocent people or attacking and destroying unsuspecting Republic targets. On Kuar, Qel-Droma gained the Mandalorian warrior clans as an army, but showed respect to their leader whom he had defeated in combat, and eventually made him his most trusted lieutenant. Although he was in turn a subordinate of Exar Kun, Qel-Droma held little regard for Kun's plan of action for the war on the Republic, and willfully disobeyed it by directly attacking Coruscant.<ref name="TSW1" /> What he did hold in high regard were the Sith goals during the Great Sith War, as he believed that a Sith victory would lead to a new golden age in the galaxy and saw the Republic as ineffectual and outdated.<ref name="TSW2" /> Qel-Droma's feelings toward his former Jedi friends also changed. Though he still tried to avoid violence with them, he was much more hostile and would fight them if need be&mdash;he became capable of directing massive amounts of rage at them, so much so that he killed his brother Cay on Ossus.<ref name="TSW5" /> He developed a sort of disdain for them, seeing them as cowards who were trying to interfere with his work. The Jedi-turned-Sith grew ever more defiant, and even went so far as to denounce the Republic during his trial in the Galactic Senate and insult the Supreme Chancellor himself to his face.<ref name="TSW3" /> Qel-Droma showed himself to be quite cunning during the Sith War, as he helped to engineer the plot to both create the Cron Supernova and eliminate Crado and Aleema Keto.<ref name="TSW4" />

===A changed man===
{{Quote|Cold&hellip; cold&hellip; my heart is like the ice around me. Why won't it just stop beating?|Ulic Qel-Droma, in the ice chasm|<ref name="redemption2" />}}
[[File:SadUlic.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Ulic Qel-Droma, blind to the Force]]
However, all of those traits were wiped away the moment that Qel-Droma struck his brother Cay down. Qel-Droma became a figure wracked by grief, for the death of his brother, the loss of his Jedi powers, the destruction of his relationships with his friends,<ref name="TSW6" /> and for his role in the Sith War&mdash;he no longer enjoyed his memories.<ref name="redemption3" /> For years, Qel-Droma struggled to come to terms with his past and the loss of his connection to the Force, and he became filled with a restlessness and lack of peace that drove him to wander the galaxy for a decade. Qel-Droma felt the need to run from his past, which drove him to isolate himself on Rhen Var and hope that the galaxy would forget his actions.<ref name="redemption1" /> Qel-Droma's mental state deteriorated on Rhen Var, as he still could not find peace; it grew worse in the ice chasm, where he was left to reflect on the worst parts of his past. At that darkest point, Qel-Droma wished that he would die, although he was convinced otherwise by the spirit of Arca Jeth. Even after all that had happened, the former Jedi still possessed considerable will and inner strength, which allowed him to escape the chasm even though he still questioned his purpose in life afterward.<ref name="redemption2" /> Ten years after his Master's death, Qel-Droma still revered Jeth and sought to find a suitable way to honor him, achieving this by carving his likeness into the side of an ice mountain with his lightsaber.<ref name="redemption4" />

Although Qel-Droma was once noted for his confidence and faith in himself,<ref name="totjcompanion" /> he lost these with his Force powers&mdash;which led him to be somewhat hostile initially to Vima Sunrider, as he believed that she was crazy for thinking that he could teach her anything about the Force.<ref name="redemption3" /> Qel-Droma deeply desired to become a Jedi again,<ref name="redemption4" /> and while he and the young Sunrider got off on the wrong foot, Qel-Droma still showed a considerable amount of compassion for her by rescuing her from a dangerous snowstorm on her first day on Rhen Var. Qel-Droma saw much of Nomi Sunrider in his future apprentice, especially in her stubbornness.<ref name="redemption3" /> Qel-Droma was extremely impressed with Sunrider's progress as a Jedi student and thought she was better than he deserved. Qel-Droma believed that he could not teach her due to his lack of a Force connection, comparing his situation to a blinded painter, only to be convinced otherwise by his charge.<ref name="redemption4" /> Qel-Droma eventually took a shine to Vima Sunrider, and even forgave her for joking about his dark side past. Through his tutelage of the young Sunrider, the former Jedi was able to find a purpose in life, which helped him to finally put his past behind him, overcome his guilt and gain a semblance of peace. These changes to his psyche allowed him to bring the same serenity to Sylvar, who was also struggling to move on from her mate Crado's death. Although he was killed shortly after his duel with Sylvar, Qel-Droma was forgiven for his past actions by Nomi Sunrider, which allowed him to die at peace.<ref name="redemption5" />

==Relationships==
===Nomi Sunrider===
{{Quote|Ulic and Nomi Sunrider seem to be enjoying one another, Master Arca.|Cay Qel-Droma|<ref name="Daudio" />}}
[[File:Nomi_Ulic_kiss.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Ulic Qel-Droma and Nomi Sunrider in a romantic moment]]
Ulic Qel-Droma first met Nomi Sunrider while observing the field of battle after the second major clash of the Freedon Nadd Uprising. Sunrider had been felled by a Force attack directed at her by King Ommin, and the sight of a beautiful young Jedi injured in battle affected Qel-Droma, who immediately went to help her recover. Although Sunrider was still groggy, Qel-Droma was able to rally her to fight alongside him during the siege of Iziz. Along with five other Knights, Qel-Droma and Sunrider battled their way together to Ommin's subterranean fortress. There, they battled and defeated Ommin side-by-side, and later attended the funeral of the Naddist leaders on Dxun.<ref name="uprising2" /> Over the next two years, Qel-Droma and Sunrider took a liking to one another, as they spent their time learning to fly Onderonian warbeasts together. In 3,997 BBY, the two Jedi were sent to battle the Krath in the Empress Teta system,<ref name="DLotS1" /> and along with Captain Orley Vanicus, took command of the Republic warship ''Reliance''. It was on the ''Reliance'' that they fought the Krath for the first time near Empress Teta, where Qel-Droma was grievously injured by a piece of shrapnel in the Republic's eye-opening defeat. The incident drove Sunrider to tears, and she ended up helping the Jedi Knight recover from his wound.<ref name="DLotS2" /> After being nursed back to health, Qel-Droma attended the Conclave on Deneba with his friend Sunrider, and the pair addressed the assembled Jedi Knights on their experiences at Empress Teta.<ref name="DLotS3" />

Qel-Droma's revered Master, Arca Jeth, was killed in the battle following the Jedi convocation, and Sunrider was the first one to comfort Qel-Droma on the loss of his mentor. Although Sunrider did not necessarily approve of Qel-Droma's plan,<ref name="DLotS3" /> she helped him prepare for his journey of infiltrating the Krath. By this time, a romantic attraction had developed between the two&mdash;as Sunrider escorted Qel-Droma to the ship that would take him to Empress Teta, the pair shared a passionate kiss.<ref name="DLotS4" /> It wouldn't be long before they met again, when a worried Sunrider traveled to Cinnagar to establish contact with him. She was captured by the Krath, and while conflicted, Qel-Droma was forced to volunteer to execute her in order to stay undercover. He never intended to carry out the deed, as he believed that Sunrider would find a way to escape, which she promptly did. Qel-Droma struck down Satal Keto during the Krath leader's confrontation with Sunrider, Cay Qel-Droma, and Tott Doneeta, but with his Sith poison amplifying his rage, he lost control and attacked the three Jedi with the Force when they tried to convince him to leave the planet with them. Although Sunrider did not want to leave him behind, she and the other Jedi fled the planet in the ''Nebulon Ranger'', and the two young lovers were separated again.<ref name="DLotS5" />

Sunrider refused to give up on Qel-Droma, but when she led a Jedi assault team on Cinnagar to retrieve him, Qel-Droma declined to go with her, as he preferred to stay on Empress Teta to finish his work. When pressed on the issue, a furious Qel-Droma lashed out at Sunrider and the other Jedi with a Sith amulet, and though Cay and several others were able to forcibly restrain Qel-Droma, Sunrider ordered them to leave him be. Qel-Droma was allowed to stay in Cinnagar with the Krath, but the violent exchange drove a wall between him and Sunrider.<ref name="DLotS6" /> Qel-Droma and Sunrider next encountered one another under extremely different pretenses&mdash;Qel-Droma, now a fully-fledged Sith Lord, led an assault on Coruscant, but was left behind by Aleema Keto. Sunrider and several other Jedi stormed the Republic war room and took Qel-Droma prisoner.<ref name="TSW2" /> Qel-Droma was put on trial for his crimes against the Republic in the Galactic Senate, a proceeding which Sunrider went on to attend. Shocked by the things that Qel-Droma said during the trial, Sunrider stormed the Senate floor when Exar Kun arrived to break his apprentice out. Qel-Droma responded by threatening his former love with violence, and escaped with Kun.<ref name="TSW3" /> Although Qel-Droma had effectively destroyed any relationship with Sunrider, thoughts of Sunrider still troubled the Sith Lord, and he still had feelings for her.<ref name="TSW4" />

Meanwhile, Qel-Droma fell deeper and deeper into the clutches of the dark side, and eventually went to Ossus with Kun to raid the Great Jedi Library's treasures ahead of the Cron Supernova shockwave. Sunrider was initially overjoyed, as she thought that Qel-Droma had returned to the Jedi side,<ref name="TSW5" /> but that all changed when she witnessed Qel-Droma strike his brother Cay down. Although Qel-Droma was overcome with guilt for his actions, Sunrider used a wall of light to strip her former love of his connection to the Force. Qel-Droma recovered enough to lead Sunrider and the Jedi to Kun's hideout on Yavin 4,<ref name="TSW6" /> but the two lost contact after the war as Qel-Droma wandered the galaxy.<ref name="redemption1" /> Sunrider went on to become a highly prominent Jedi Master, but neglected her daughter Vima's Jedi training, which led Vima to seek out Qel-Droma to train her in the Force. After Qel-Droma taught Vima for a time and bonded with his young apprentice, Nomi came to Qel-Droma's hideout on Rhen Var to retrieve her daughter. Qel-Droma and Nomi stood face-to-face for the first time in years and discussed Vima's future&mdash;although Vima was vehement in her desire to stay with Qel-Droma, the former Jedi Knight left the decision to Nomi. Qel-Droma's worth as a teacher was proven to Nomi when Vima showed her the ice sculptures that they had made together; while they went off together to look at the works, Qel-Droma engaged in his fateful duel with Sylvar. Qel-Droma was shot and killed by Hoggon as the two Sunriders arrived on the scene, and as he died, he was forgiven for his past actions by his former love. Qel-Droma died in Nomi Sunrider's arms, and shocked her when his body disappeared as he passed to the Netherworld of the Force.<ref name="redemption5" />

===Aleema Keto===
{{Quote|I'm enjoying our contest, but I'm winning too easily, Ulic. Perhaps I want you to be stronger. Perhaps I'd like to be conquered.|Aleema Keto, to Ulic Qel-Droma|audio=AleemaKetoSeducingAJedi-DLOTS.flac|<ref name="Daudio" />}}
[[File:UlicAleema-bedroom.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Ulic Qel-Droma and Aleema Keto, having just made love]]
Qel-Droma's first encounter with Aleema Keto came on Empress Teta in 3,997 BBY, during his mission to infiltrate the Krath. Posing as a fallen Jedi, Qel-Droma rescued the dark side sorceress from an assassination attempt, an action which caught Keto's eye.<ref name="DLotS4" /> However, the cunning magician promptly drugged Qel-Droma and imprisoned him below the Iron Citadel, where the Jedi Knight was injected with Satal Keto's Sith poison and incapacitated. After that ordeal was over, Qel-Droma and Keto entered into a romantic relationship&mdash;Qel-Droma sensed the desire that Keto felt for him, and sought to use it, and her, as a means to conquer the dark side. On the other hand, Keto had seen through Qel-Droma's ruse all along and meant to use the Jedi Knight for her own purposes, and she worked to undermine Qel-Droma's determination and adherence to the Jedi way through their mutual attraction.<ref name="DLotS5" /> Their relationship grew more serious, and Keto, who saw it as a "contest," one day gave Qel-Droma a powerful Sith amulet, and expressed her desire to be conquered. A Jedi team soon arrived to retrieve Qel-Droma, but he decided to stay in Cinnagar with Keto over leaving with his former friends. After Qel-Droma joined forces with Exar Kun as Kun's Sith apprentice, the now-former Jedi Knight allowed his new lover Keto to serve alongside him in the coming war with the Republic.<ref name="DLotS6" />

As the war began, Qel-Droma made Keto his top advisor and used Keto's powers of illusion to great effect during his raid on the Foerost shipyards.<ref name="TSW1" /> In an unexpected twist, Keto betrayed Qel-Droma during his assault on Coruscant, as she ordered his support forces to fall back and leave him to the Jedi.<ref name="TSW2" /> Qel-Droma escaped Republic custody, however, and when he returned into the arms of the Sith, he was informed by Mandalore the Indomitable that it was indeed Aleema Keto who had allowed him to be captured. It was then that Qel-Droma realized that Keto had manipulated him ever since they first met, and he resolved to eliminate her. He and Kun planned for Keto's death, which they soon brought about during the attack on Kemplex Nine&mdash;it was only in her final moments that Keto realized her treachery had been discovered.<ref name="TSW4" /> Although Qel-Droma was rid of the person who had betrayed him, thoughts of Keto still weighed heavily upon him during the subsequent raid on Ossus.<ref name="TSW5" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|I'm like an artist who's been blinded. I can no longer see to paint.|Ulic Qel-Droma, reflecting on his powerless state|<ref name="redemption4" />}}
[[File:DarkSideUlic.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Ulic Qel-Droma]]

===Lightsaber Combat===
In battle, Qel-Droma was an exceptionally skilled lightsaber wielder, specializing in the [[Form V/Legends|Djem So]] form.<ref name="kotorcg" /> His skills were aided by his great agility,<ref name="beastwars1" /> and lightning-fast reflexes,.<ref name="DLotS5" /> He was highly accurate with his attacks, and highly proficient in both single combat and handling multiple opponents. Qel-Droma also proved proficient in fighting with a group, effectively coordinating with a Jedi assault team during the Freedon Nadd Uprising<ref name="uprising2" /> and with a Sith one during his ill-fated attack on Coruscant in 3996 BBY.<ref name="DLotS2" /> Although Djem So wasn't an acrobatic form, Ulic proved proficient in using acrobatic lightsaber attacks, indicating he was familiar with Ataru, and he repeatedly displayed great prowess in defensive techniques, particularly in blast-deflection, succeeding even in comprised situations, showing he was well-versed with either Soresu or Shien.

During his defense of the Iziz Royal Palace, he single-handedly battled dozens of Beast Riders at the same time, and even slew one of their war mounts.<ref name="beastwars1" /> Even while pressured by the pall of the dark side, Qel-Droma was not only able to defeat the Dark Jedi Warb Null even while oppressed by the pall of the dark side,<ref name="uprising1" /> but he was able to fight even the tremendously skilled Exar Kun, who was able to slay even his great Jedi master in a duel, to a stalemate, a feat that no one else was ever able to replicate, with even the arrogant Exar Kun being impressed and admitting that Qel-Droma was a skilled duelist indeed.<ref name="DLotS6" />

As a Sith, he defeated Mandalore in a duel rigged for the mando, thus gaining the loyalty of the clans.<ref name="TSW1" /> Later he killed his [[Cay Qel-Droma|brother]] in a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|duel]], though he instantly regretted slaying his kin and did nothing as his Force Powers were completely removed from him by Nomi Sunrider.<ref name="TSW5" /> However, even without the Force to guide him, Qel-Droma still retained his skills in lightsaber combat,<ref name="redemption2" />&mdash; with him still being able to feel and wield his blade effectively even though his ability to sense the Force was gone.<ref name="redemption4" /> Despite having spent years in exile, he remained a formidable duelist and managed to defend himself successfully against all of [[Sylvar]]'s fury-driven attacks.<ref name="redemption5" />

===Force Powers===
[[File:UlicQel-Droma-FF.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Ulic Qel-Droma corrupted by the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]].]]
Although his training was neglected during his youth, Ulic Qel-Droma possessed a considerable natural talent in the Force. A voracious learner, the prodigal Qel-Droma easily and quickly mastered the basic techniques taught to him on Arkania by Master Arca Jeth.<ref name="totjcompanion" /> He was regarded as the greatest Jedi Knight of his time, and as a Sith Lord, Freedon Nadd's spirit believed he would have the potential to be among the greatest Sith Lords in history, considered to be capable of challenging even Exar Kun and being second only to him in terms of Force strength.

Though he was a novice in terms of dealing with the dark side, lacking the ability to quickly sense its presence during years under Jeth's tutelage,<ref name="beastwars2" /> and never learning to distinguish dark illusions from real life,<ref name="DLotS2" /> Ulic was adept in defensive skills, capable of creating [[Force barrier/Legends|barriers]] strong enough to repel blasts from the laser cannon of a Basilisk War Droid and drawing upon the light in order to overcome dark attacks, killing the likes of Null and Ommin with ease after neutralizing their attempts to subdue him with the dark side.<ref name="uprising2" /> He also possessed the ability to see through the Force, allowing him to handle himself in situations where his eyes were of no use to him, and with training, he became very proficient in using the Force to predict attacks.<ref name="audio" /> After continuing his later Jedi training, Ulic became proficient with [[Mind trick/Legends|mind tricks]], acknowledged by his friend and fellow Arca Jeth apprentice, Tott Doneeta, in his great growth at the ability, easily compelling two beast riders into disarming themselves and telling him about the situation.

When he joined the Krath, Qel-Droma was injected with a Sith poison, which amplified his [[Force Enrage|rage]] and granted him immense dark side power in the form of a [[Force scream/Legends|Force scream]] that destoyed a small pillar of stone and the torture droid that tormented him, and later used this power to drive off Nomi, Cay, and Tott. He became capable of unleashing bursts of dark energy, which could blow his opponents off their feet. Qel-Droma could use [[Force stealth]] to hide his true thoughts or loyalties.<ref name="DLotS5" /> On Empress Teta, Qel-Droma was given a [[Sith talisman/Legends|Sith amulet]] by his new flame, Aleema Keto&mdash;he learned how to use the Sith treasure to attack enemies with [[Color/Legends|blue-hued]] [[Force blast|dark energy]], and used it against his former Jedi friends in the Iron Citadel.<ref name="DLotS6" /> By the time of the Sith War, Qel-Droma had begun to use the dark side with great skill,<ref name="TSW1" /> including such powers as [[Qâzoi Kyantuska|Control Mind]] and Force choke.<ref name="TSW2" /> By drawing upon the dark side, he became even more quick and agile, able to dodge dozens of blaster bolts at the same time.<ref name="TSW1" /> Even with all this dark power, during his [[Battle of Coruscant (Great Sith War)|raid on the capital of the Republic]] Ulric's saber was torn from his hand with the Force and he was captured in a small wall of light, showing that his [[Force barrier/Legends|Force shield]] was not perfect.<ref name="TSW2" />

After the death of his brother on Ossus, Qel-Droma was completely stripped of his connection to the Force when Nomi Sunrider punished him by destroying his connection to the Force by employing [[Sever Force/Legends|sever Force]]. Although he valiantly searched for a way to repair the loss of his Jedi powers, there was none to be found.<ref name="TSW6" /> Although he could no longer manipluate the Force in life, upon his death, his body disappeared like those of the Jedi Masters.<ref name="redemption5" /> He also gained the ability, after his death, to return to the mortal world as a Force ghost.<ref name="Clone Wars" />

===Other Abilities===
Ulic was a ferocious [[Unarmed combat/Legends|hand-to-hand fighter]], able to best the mighty Mandalore even while highly disadvantaged.<ref name="TSW1" /> However, he was not infallible in combat, as he was very nearly defeated by a Krath war droid during the Battle of Deneba, only to be saved by Jeth.<ref name="DLotS3" /> An able pilot, Qel-Droma was able to fly a ship through large groups of enemies without taking damage,<ref name="beastwars1" /> and he was adept in one-on-one [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfights]].<ref name="TSW5" /> He also possessed some skill in riding animals, as he once traveled through the Onderonian forests on a boma beast,<ref name="beastwars2" /> and later learned how to fly on the war mounts favored by the Beast Rider clans.<ref name="DLotS1" /> He additionally possessed some knowledge of first aid and healing, as shown when he treated his brother Cay's wounds after he lost his arm in the Iziz Royal Palace.<ref name="audio" />

Ulic was a remarkably intelligent man. A capable negotiator, he was able to get the stubborn Kiras to agree to his plan to make peace with the Onderonian monarchy&mdash;however, he was not good enough to convince Queen Amanoa to reciprocate.<ref name="beastwars2" /> During the first battle with the Krath near Empress Teta, Qel-Droma tried his hand at commanding a fleet, only to be met with defeat.<ref name="DLotS2" /> He would be more successful during the Sith War, and led his forces to many successful raids on Republic targets.<ref name="TSW1" /> A confident public speaker, Qel-Droma was able to formulate complex plans of action, including those of his infiltration of the Krath<ref name="DLotS3" /> and for the attack on Coruscant during the Sith War. He could be quite cunning, as evidenced by his distraction of the Republic fleet before his assault on Coruscant<ref name="TSW2" /> and by his betrayal of Aleema Keto.<ref name="TSW4" />

Qel-Droma was multilingual, able to speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic]], [[Twi'leki/Legends|Twi'leki]], [[Arkanian (language)/Legends|Arkanian]], and [[Sith (language)|Sith]].<ref name="dssourcebook" /> Despite having spent years in exile, Ulic proved himself to be a competent teachers in the ways of a Jedi, and successfully taught Vima Sunrider. With Sunrider's help, Qel-Droma himself learned how to use his natural talent to accomplish feats like creating sculptures, without relying on the Force like he once had.

He also retained a great amount of strength, both inner and physical, even in a depressed and weakened state.<ref name="redemption2" />

==Equipment==
Qel-Droma wielded two lightsabers over the course of his life. The first was a single-bladed lightsaber with a green blade and a unique emitter made up of four spikes (similar to his brother Cay's). The second light saber was also a single-bladed lightsaber, however with a yellow blade, which stayed fully operational years after he lost his Jedi powers.<ref name="redemption2" /> He favored [[link armor]] such as the [[SupraLink]] [[Armor/Legends|armor]] manufactured by [[ProTech]].<ref name="totjcompanion" /> In battle, he often wore a [[Ulic Qel-Droma's mesh suit|mesh suit]], which he later cast aside after the end of the Great Sith War.<ref name="kotor2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|There's somewhat of a connection to Luke. As a matter of fact, Ulic is sort of an anagram of Luke. This guy ends up going totally over to the dark side. So the idea is, we take the young, idealistic hero, don't make him look like Skywalker, make him a different person, but the definite type&mdash;the impulsive, young warrior who's very sure of himself.|Tom Veitch, to interviewer Ilene Rosenberg|<ref name="makingswc" />}}
The character of Ulic Qel-Droma first appeared in [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Ulic Qel-Droma and the Beast Wars of Onderon|''Ulic Qel-Droma and the Beast Wars of Onderon'']], the first story arc of the [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series, written by [[Tom Veitch]] and released in [[1993]].<ref name="beastwars1" /> Although ''Beast Wars'' was Qel-Droma's first actual appearance, he was first mentioned in Veitch's [[Dark Empire endnotes|endnotes]] for the ''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]'' series released earlier.<ref name="endnotes" /> Qel-Droma was the protagonist of much of the ''Tales of the Jedi'' comics. He was heavily featured in the subsequent arcs [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising|''The Freedon Nadd Uprising'']],<ref name="uprising1" /> [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith|''Dark Lords of the Sith'']],<ref name="DLotS1" /> [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War|''The Sith War'']],<ref name="TSW1" /> and [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Redemption|''Redemption'']], where his story was concluded and the character killed.<ref name="redemption5" /> Qel-Droma was also portrayed in the audio dramas of the [[Tales of the Jedi (audio drama)|earlier ''Tales of the Jedi'' arcs]],<ref name="audio" /> and of [[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|''Dark Lords of the Sith'']].<ref name="Daudio" /> During his appearances in the comics, he was illustrated by several different artists: [[Chris Gossett]],<ref name="beastwars1" /> [[Tony Akins]],<ref name="uprising1" /> [[Art Wetherell]],<ref name="DLotS6" /> and [[Dario Carrasco, Jr.]]<ref name="TSW1" />

[[File:UlicQelDroma-NEGTC.png|thumb|right|120px|Ulic Qel-Droma]]
In the ''Tales of the Jedi'' audio drama, Qel-Droma was voiced by [[David Scott Gordon]],<ref name="audio" /> while he was portrayed by [[John Cygan]] in the ''Dark Lords of the Sith'' adaptation.<ref name="Daudio" /> Qel-Droma later appeared as a Force ghost in [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (video game)|''The Clone Wars'']] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] in [[2002]], where he was voiced by [[Charles Dennis]].<ref name="Clone Wars" />

In various interviews, the authors who helped make ''Tales of the Jedi'' have revealed information about the origins and development of Ulic Qel-Droma. Tom Veitch has indicated that the ''Tales of the Jedi'' characters, including Qel-Droma, were created by him and his collaborators, before being approved by [[Lucasfilm]]. Veitch originally wrote a different conclusion to Qel-Droma's story than what ended up appearing in ''Tales of the Jedi: Redemption'', preferring his ending to what appeared in the comics.<ref name="veitch">[[Wookieepedia:Interview/Tom Veitch|Interview with Tom Veitch]]</ref> Veitch, who wrote the ''Dark Empire'' endnotes in which the character was first mentioned,<ref name="endnotes" /> told interviewer [[Ilene Rosenberg]] in [[1994]] that the writers of ''Tales of the Jedi'' made Qel-Droma as a sort of mirror image of ''[[Star Wars]]'' movie hero Luke Skywalker.<ref name="makingswc" /> [[Chris Gossett]], the penciller for several ''Tales of the Jedi'' arcs, revealed in a correspondence with the ''Star Wars'' fan site [[Wookieepedia]] that he was the one who originally designed Qel-Droma, along with many other characters and objects from the comic arcs&mdash;in fact, Qel-Droma was the first character that Gossett ever designed professionally.<ref name="gossett">[[Wookieepedia:Interview/Christian Gossett|Interview with Christian Gossett]]</ref> [[Kevin J. Anderson]], a writer who worked alongside Veitch during the creation of ''Tales of the Jedi'', divulged that Qel-Droma's ultimate fate was already decided before the ''Redemption'' arc was written and that his death was their decision.<ref name="kja">[[Wookieepedia:Interview/Kevin J. Anderson|Interview with Kevin J. Anderson]]</ref>

Cut content from ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' would have featured ruins named after the Qel-Droma family on Alderaan, with the Upper Ruins and Lower Ruins containing a Republic and Imperial landing area respectively.

===Continuity===
[[File:Ulic_Qel-Droma_KOTORCG.jpg|thumb|180px|Ulic Qel-Droma]]
There have been several continuity issues regarding the events of Ulic Qel-Droma's life. Many of these&mdash;mostly small changes in dialogue or in the sequence of events in the Beast Wars&mdash;come from differences between the story of the ''Tales of the Jedi'' comics and those of their various audio adaptations. In all cases where these two sources conflict, the comics are treated with superior [[canon]]icity in this article. More continuity differences arise from the comics and the earlier ''Dark Empire'' endnotes. For example, the endnotes state that Qel-Droma reached the rank of Jedi Master, although during the comic retelling of his life, he never became a Master. Once again, the comics are treated with superior canonicity in these particular situations. In ''The Clone Wars'' video game, a representation of Ulic Qel-Droma appears to Anakin Skywalker; there are several sources that differ on whether the form that appeared to Skywalker was Qel-Droma's Force ghost, or a simple hologram. While the Dark Reaper entry in ''The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia'' treats the apparition as a hologram, the ''Encyclopedia''{{'s}} Force Harvester entry and ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' say that it was indeed Qel-Droma's spirit. For the purposes of this article, the latter option is treated as correct.

Another major continuity issue is centered around the color of Ulic Qel-Droma's lightsaber. In various illustrations, Qel-Droma's lightsaber appears with no fewer than four different hues. Yellow and blue are the most common, alternately appearing in different ''Tales of the Jedi'' arcs and comics. However, the lightsaber has also been shown with a red blade and with a green blade on ''Tales of the Jedi'' covers. Additionally, the color of the weapon differs in several reference books, such as ''The New Essential Chronology'' and ''The New Essential Guide to Characters''. Qel-Droma's [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry confirms that he wielded lightsabers with different blade colors throughout his life.<ref name="databank" />
